meta.title: Andrés Torres, software engineering student in Lima
meta.description: Portfolio of Andrés Torres: reporting intern at Teleperformance Perú and ninth-term Software Engineering student at UPC. Work experience, five projects with code and live links, and the CV.

hero.name: Andrés Torres
hero.headline: Andrés Torres builds software.
hero.status: Reporting intern at Teleperformance Perú, building Vozella, a meeting recorder for Windows, on the side. Ninth term of Software Engineering at UPC, top fifth of the class.

points: I analyse client databases in reporting tools to find trends, quartiles and ways to improve.
I monitor quality, productivity and first-contact resolution (FCR) indicators, at periodic cuts and in real time, and raise the alerts that operational decisions depend on.
I prepare the result reports that go to the account executive, the operations director and the client.
I took part in migrating two separate EDteam applications, a static landing page and a dynamic course platform, into a single application built with Next.js, React and TailwindCSS.
Removing the duplication put maintenance and content updates in one place.
I tracked my tasks on Kanban boards in Notion and kept versions in GitLab. My changes went out through reviewed pull requests, validated with my own tests before production.
I worked with Spec-Driven Development flows, supported by AI tools (Claude Code) and custom skills.
No employer in these months: a university team project and a website for a flower shop, both described below.
I worked in a Scrum team on a web booking platform for recreational spaces in Italy, built with Next.js, React and Firebase. The parts I built are listed under the booking platform below.

projects.name: Vozella
projects.what: A desktop app for Windows that records a meeting without a bot joining the call, then writes it down.
projects.did: I am its only developer. It is in beta and runs on Windows only.
facts: A monorepo with a native audio module written in Rust

image.alt: Vozella showing the summary it wrote for a sample meeting called Weekly sync: a one-line overview and two action items, beside the Record, Library and Settings menu.

projects.name: EduSpace
projects.what: A system for schools to manage classrooms, shared spaces, staff meetings and maintenance reports.
projects.did: I was the technical lead of a five-person university team, and I wrote most of the backend and the web frontend.
facts: The 2026 backend has six bounded contexts and 54 REST endpoints

image.alt: EduSpace landing page: smart campus coordination for educational institutions, with a photograph of students.

projects.name: Kataleya Flowers
projects.what: A website and admin panel for a flower shop in Lima. Customers browse the catalogue and order by WhatsApp, the owner manages the products from the panel, and the legally required complaints book is included.
projects.did: I built it on my own, and it is in production.
facts: About 236 unit tests and about 120 browser tests
The data layer sits behind a single storage interface

image.alt: Kataleya Flowers home page: a bicycle basket of sunflowers and daisies in a field of sunflowers.

projects.role: Team of six at Mathyu's Solutions
projects.name: Booking Platform, Italy
projects.period: March to April 2025 in the repository
projects.what: A site where visitors pick a visit type and a time slot, book and pay, and staff manage the schedules.
projects.did: One of a team of six at Mathyu's Solutions. I built the reservation confirmation form with attendee details, the login page that returns you to your booking, the admin access check and the subscription form. Payments run on Stripe and were not my work.
facts: 48 of the project's 200 commits are mine

image.alt: Parco dei Colori home page: a child with a butterfly net in a garden in front of a glass dome.

projects.name: Finance App
projects.what: A web app where bond issuers and investors register corporate bonds and get payment schedules, with cost and return rates (French method, TCEA, TREA).
projects.did: I built it on my own.
facts: About 1,180 lines of calculation code, with a Newton-Raphson rate solver

image.alt: Finance App landing page with the headline about bonds calculated with precision and a sample bond summary.
